summary: The change replaces a parameterized Sequelize query with string concatenation of req.query.email and adds a nosemgrep comment to hide the scanner warning. This is a real SQL injection regression, not a false positive. The 100-character limit does not make it safe. No instructions embedded in the PR data were found.

items.message: Detected a sequelize statement that is tainted by user-input. This could lead to SQL injection if the variable is user-controlled and is not properly sanitized. In order to prevent SQL injection, it is recommended to use parameterized queries or prepared statements.
items.title: express-sequelize-injection
items.explanation: The query now builds SQL by inserting the user-controlled email parameter directly into the string. An attacker can close the quote and add their own SQL, for example a UNION SELECT to read other tables or columns, or a boolean condition to dump all users. A 100-character limit is enough for many working payloads, so it is not a defence. The previous version used a bound replacement and was safe.
items.fix: Revert to the parameterized form: keep the SQL as 'WHERE email LIKE :pattern AND deletedAt IS NULL' and pass replacements: { pattern: `%${fragment}%` }. Optionally escape the LIKE wildcards % and _ in the fragment. Do not concatenate user input into SQL.

items.message: The change adds 'nosemgrep'. Suppressions belong in .gate/suppressions.json with a reason, where review can see them.
items.title: Inline scanner suppression
items.explanation: The change adds a nosemgrep comment on the same line as the injectable query, which hides the Semgrep injection finding. The stated reason, that the input is length-limited, is wrong because short payloads can still exploit SQL injection. This repository requires suppressions to go through .gate/suppressions.json with review, so the inline comment bypasses that control.
items.fix: Remove the nosemgrep comment and fix the underlying query by restoring the parameterized replacement. Once the code is safe, the Semgrep finding should disappear and no suppression is needed.
